description:
src/methods/event_copy.rs:16-36 takes `create: serde_json::Value` with no validation. RFC 8620 §5.4 (referenced by draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.7) says `create` is "Map<Id, T>" — a JSON object whose keys are caller-chosen creation ids and whose values are partial T objects.

If a caller passes `json!("hello")` or `json!([])` or `json!(null)`, we send a bad request to the server. Server will reject with `invalidArguments`, but the client could do better.

More importantly: the documented argument `fromAccountId: &str` has an empty guard, but `accountId` (the destination, looked up from the session) does not — and `create` has no shape validation at all. The empty-guard pattern is partial and inconsistent.

Suggested fix: either type `create` as a builder/struct (CopyRequest in PLAN.md §A.4) or at minimum require `create.is_object()` before sending and return InvalidArgument otherwise. Keeps the bad-input failure local and gives a better error message than 'server returned invalidArguments at /create.'
title: calendar_event_copy: from_account_id is the only Id arg with empty-guard, accepts arbitrary content for create
